context: The standard greeting all day until early evening. Always say it when entering a shop.
Replaces 'bonjour' from early evening (around 6 PM).
Informal: friends, family and people your age. Works for hello and goodbye.
Polite goodbye for any situation.
'Merci' alone is also fine; 'beaucoup' adds warmth.
Casual reply to 'merci'. A more formal option is 'je vous en prie'.
Formal/polite form. With friends you say 's'il te plaît'.
To get someone's attention or to get past someone politely.
Quick apology (e.g. bumping into someone) or asking someone to repeat.
Friendly everyday question. Often shortened to 'Ça va ?'.

front: Ça va bien, merci. Et vous ?
context: Standard answer. Use 'et toi ?' with friends.
Literally 'I call myself Anna'. Replace the name with yours.
Written 'enchantée' when a woman says it; the pronunciation is the same.
In speech the 'ne' is often dropped: 'Je comprends pas'.

front: Vous pouvez répéter, s'il vous plaît ?
context: Your best friend as a beginner. Add 'plus lentement' to ask for slower speech.
Rising intonation turns a statement into a question.
'Toilettes' is always plural in French.
Point at the item and ask. Very common in markets and shops.

front: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-DREH an kah-FAY, seel voo PLEH]
back: I would like a coffee, please.
context: 'Je voudrais' is the polite way to order. 'Un café' is an espresso.
Waiters in France won't bring the bill until you ask for it.
